methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective design on 106 consecutive R0-resected, neoadjuvant-naive gastric adenocarcinoma cases with >=61 months follow-up is appropriate for exploring prognostic correlations. IHC for CD163/CD34 used standardized antibodies and automated platforms, with dual blinded pathologist assessment per International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group recommendations, and median-based dichotomization to avoid overfitting. However, the Cox multivariable model includes only four a priori covariates and omits other established prognostic variables (grading, angiolymphatic/perineural invasion, Lauren type), and the reported 95% CIs contain negative bounds for HRs (e.g., pT: 3.6 [0.19–2.35]; MVD: 0.97 [-0.05 to -0.002]), suggesting the intervals reported are on the log-HR or beta scale rather than proper HR CIs — a reporting error that undermines interpretability.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single-center retrospective observational cohort of 106 patients, corresponding to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort / case series without control group). Findings corroborate the known M2-TAM/angiogenesis axis at the invasive front and add a counterintuitive observation of MVD as a favorable independent prognostic factor. While biologically interesting, the result is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before influencing practice.

reporting_quality.justification: As a tumor biomarker prognostic study, REMARK is the most relevant reporting standard. Patient selection, IHC methods, blinding, and statistical approach are adequately described, and Kaplan-Meier/Cox analyses follow standard workflow. However, REMARK is not explicitly referenced, STROBE is also not mentioned, and key REMARK items are incomplete: no sample-size justification, incomplete clinicopathological table detail in-text, ambiguous CI reporting for HRs, and no data or code availability statement is provided.

novelty_literature.justification: The association of M2 TAMs with angiogenesis and invasion depth at the gastric cancer invasive front has been shown previously by Wu et al. 2012, Park et al. 2016, and Zhang et al. 2025, which the authors acknowledge. The one genuinely unexpected finding — that higher MVD at the invasive front is an independent favorable prognostic factor — runs counter to the 4094-patient Hong et al. meta-analysis and is interesting but based on a single small cohort and may partially reflect methodological choices. Overall, incremental confirmation with one intriguing anomaly.

writing_presentation.justification: The text is organized and readable with a clear IMRaD structure. The Discussion is thorough and comparative across multiple prior studies. However, the paper is very discussion-heavy relative to its results, some passages drift into tangential topics (lung cancer metabolic reprogramming, CH25H), and the CI reporting error for Cox HRs is a material presentation flaw that requires correction before publication.

key_strengths: Adequate cohort size (n=106) of uniformly R0-resected, neoadjuvant-naive gastric cancers with long follow-up (>=61 months)
Standardized IHC with dual blinded pathologist scoring and adherence to International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group invasive-front definition
Use of a priori covariate selection and median-based dichotomization to reduce overfitting
Intriguing and counterintuitive independent MVD-survival association that warrants further investigation
key_concerns: Confidence interval reporting for Cox hazard ratios is inconsistent (intervals contain negative values), suggesting the beta/log-HR scale was reported rather than HR CIs — requires correction
Multivariable model omits established prognostic factors (grading, Lauren type, angiolymphatic/perineural invasion) as the authors acknowledge
Single-center retrospective design without external validation limits generalizability of the unexpected MVD-positive-prognosis finding
No data/code availability statement; REMARK/STROBE checklist not explicitly followed
Findings partly replicate prior literature, limiting novelty
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but incremental retrospective biomarker study with one intriguing anomaly (MVD as favorable prognostic factor) and a material CI-reporting error; best fits a tier 3 specialty oncology journal after major revisions to correct statistics and expand covariates.
